correctness.rationale: Finite reduced commutative rings are products of finite fields. In that model, principal-ideal containment is support containment, so adjacency is support incomparability. Support fibers are exactly false-twin classes; the quotient degree formula isolates singleton/co-singleton supports, and their multiplicities recover the field orders. The side-swap equations force the all-binary case, eliminating the only apparent ambiguity.

The 2022 paper studies Laplacian spectra and Wiener indices of cozero-divisor graphs associated to rings of integers modulo \(n\).

evidence: The two-field theorem implies only the \(r=2\) structural special case.

The reduced graph identifies elements generating the same principal ideal; for products of fields it therefore retains support inclusion but discards each support fiber size \(\prod_{i\in A}(q_i-1)\).
The final theorem uses those discarded multiplicities and a new quotient reconstruction to recover all \(q_i\) for arbitrary \(r\).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existing reduced-graph decomposition results cannot imply field-order recovery because their quotient is independent of the field orders. The two-factor full-graph theorem does not determine the higher-factor quotient automorphism issue resolved here.

value.rationale: The result is a complete and natural reconstruction theorem for finite reduced nonfields. It explains exactly how multiplicities discarded by the reduced cozero-divisor graph restore all finite-field factor sizes, and it identifies the empty-graph field boundary sharply.
